extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2023 Area Chairs (ACs) / program committee members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Area Chairs at ICLR 2023 on managing the review process: bidding and reviewer assignment, moderating multi-stage discussion, organizing reviewer/AC meetings for borderline papers, handling ethics and emergency reviewers, and writing meta-reviews and final recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to key dates and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the timeline for bidding, assignments, review, discussion, virtual meetings, meta-review due dates, and author notification (specific dates listed for ICLR 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of deadlines (e.g., bidding, review period, author revision cutoff, meta-review due date). Expect small last-minute adjustments and plan responsibilities accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and enforce the Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: ICLR's Code of Ethics must be acknowledged and adhered to by all participants including authors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any submission, review, or discussion comments raise ethical concerns, flag the problematic content, collect information/evidence (from the paper, discussion with author and/or reviewers), and contact the Program Chairs. Flagged papers may be passed to the Ethics board; AC recommendation is non-binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure 3 quality reviews per paper (Reviewing Process Manager)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs should help manage reviewer assignments so every submission receives three quality reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend appropriate reviewers (or let bids determine assignments), identify delinquent reviewers, assign alternate or emergency reviewers promptly, and recruit additional reviews when they would improve confidence. If a paper lacks 3 informed reviews after the deadline, immediately start finding emergency reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vet and recommend reviewer assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: When assigned a batch, ACs should recommend a set of appropriate reviewers and vet assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may skip recommending and allow bids-only assignment, but are expected to intervene when reviewers are delinquent or unqualified. Use AC console to assign emergency reviewers and contact SACs/PCs if you struggle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and assign alternate/emergency reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek emergency/additional reviewers in two cases: unresponsive assigned reviewers past the deadline, or when additional reviews could improve confidence in a recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try to recruit emergency reviewers immediately; assign them via AC console; contact Senior AC or Program Chairs if unable to find reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision making: recommend accept/reject and write meta-review
rubrics_metrics.description: For every submission, ACs must recommend accept or reject and provide a metareview summarizing reviews and discussions, optionally adding their own view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AC recommendations should be justified based on content and discussion. Senior Area Chairs and Program Chairs will engage to help calibration; AC recommendations are influential but non-binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review content and minimum length
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reviews should clearly and thoroughly convey the recommendation and reasoning; 'Aim to write a meta-review of at least 60 words.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful meta-review items: (1) concise description of submission's main content (scientific claims, findings, strengths, weaknesses, and what's missing); (2) concise summary of discussion listing reviewer points, how authors addressed them, and whether AC found each point worth consideration; (3) clear recommendation and justification ending with the recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate discussions and discourage non-scientific/toxic comments
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs are responsible for encouraging and moderating active discussions, ensuring focus on scientific claims and merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively engage when a submission lacks attention; discourage participation irrelevant to scientific claims; moderate to prevent toxic behavior; encourage reviewers to respond to author rebuttals; identify any Code of Ethics violations during discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate as a scientific expert in discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs should actively participate in discussions not only as moderators but also as scientific experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask authors and reviewers for clarifications when needed, provide your own view of the paper, and help reach an informed decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize virtual reviewer/AC meetings for borderline papers
rubrics_metrics.description: This year ACs are required to hold a discussion meeting with reviewers for every borderline paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact reviewers (emails visible on OpenReview), schedule via tools like Doodle, consider time zones, use an online conferencing tool (e.g., Jitsi), moderate the meeting, ask all reviewers to state their view and respond to rebuttals, summarize each reviewer's comments, obtain reviewer consent on the summary, and post the summary to OpenReview noting any missing reviewers. Meetings are suggested to be ~30–40 minutes, but length/format is flexible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and identification of borderline papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Borderline papers will be determined primarily using review scores and the spread; ACs can also mark other papers they consider borderline/worth discussing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores and score spread are a good proxy to catch most borderline cases among many submissions. Historically ~3–4 borderline papers per stack; ACs may organize meetings for additional papers at their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle reviewer non-attendance in meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a majority of reviewers do not attend, ACs should encourage attendance, send reminders, and proceed if reviewers remain unresponsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send two or three reminders before proceeding without an unresponsive reviewer; note missing reviewers in the meeting summary; ACs may downweight reviews from reviewers who refuse to attend meetings (excluding emergencies). If reviewers repeatedly fail to attend, SACs will be informed for future reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize meetings and post to OpenReview
rubrics_metrics.description: After virtual meetings, ACs should summarize discussions and post the summary to OpenReview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries should include each reviewer's comments and note which reviewer was missing (if any). Use the summary to inform the meta-review and final recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for author revisions during the discussion period
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may revise their submission up until a stated date during discussions (Nov 18 for 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decisions and meta-reviews should take revisions into account, but ACs reserve the right to ignore revisions that are substantially different from the original version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to author messages via OpenReview
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may directly message ACs using OpenReview comments directed to ACs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs are expected to respond to reasonable inquiries promptly and raise issues with SACs if the answer requires further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect evidence and follow process for ethics flags
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers flag submissions for Code of Ethics violations, ACs should collect information and provide evidence when making recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully consider facts; if problematic, contact Program Chairs. Flagged papers may be escalated to the Ethics board for further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation expectations for contemporaneous work
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition for contemporaneous work: papers published within the last two months relative to the full paper deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper was published on or after two months before the deadline (e.g., July 28 for a Sept 28 deadline), authors are not required to compare their work to that paper. Refer to Reviewer Guide FAQs for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for citing non-peer-reviewed work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to cite and discuss all relevant papers, including arXiv/non-peer-reviewed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may be excused for not knowing about papers not published in peer-reviewed proceedings or journals; use judgment when evaluating completeness of citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on score distributions / curve fitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Chairs do not plan to share rating curves; ACs should base recommendations on reviews and paper quality rather than fitting to a curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to accept quality papers without being constrained by an acceptance curve. Use SACs to help calibrate if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and professionalism in reviews and meta-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure language used in reviews and AC meta-reviews is constructive and polite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to phrasing; recommended reading: Daniel Dennett, 'Criticizing with Kindness'. ACs should model professional behavior in discussions and written summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging for desk rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs can flag submissions for desk reject when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect supporting information and evidence; AC recommendations on desk rejects are non-binding and may be escalated to Ethics board or handled by SAC/PCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping about missing/unresponsive reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Note missing reviewers and unresponsiveness for future reference and program-level tracking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reviewer doesn't respond to meeting requests after 2–3 reminders, note it in the meeting summary and inform SACs/PCs as appropriate so reviewers may be marked for future reference.
